description: Cases of the T1 checks outcome.constant_clusters, outcome.minority_events, outcome.boundary_shares and outcome.zero_shares and of the T2 check outcome.separation: their decisions and messages, family filters, availability, findings for the model as a whole, binary, binomial and categorical outcomes, the tiers that a run reaches and the refusals E6069, E6078, E7007, E7008 and E7009.

cases.description: A Gaussian outcome that varies within every level of subject: constant_levels is 0, the share 0% and the message none_constant. Without a declaration, there is no disclosure unit and the by_unit counts resolve as person counts.
cases.reason: Inspect the outcome before the model is chosen.

message.text: The outcome varies within every level of 'subject' that has two or more rows.

cases.description: A binary outcome with the family binomial and no trials, so the class is bernoulli. One of the four subjects has only events, a share of exactly 25%, which reaches the threshold many. outcome.minority_events counts 9 events, 7 non-events and one level without a minority event. The median level minority count is 1, at position 2 of the sorted counts 0, 1, 2 and 2, and the minority count is divided by the 2 kept columns.
cases.reason: Inspect the outcome before the model is chosen.

message.text: The outcome is constant within 1 of the 4 levels of 'subject' with two or more rows (25%). For a binary outcome, this can push the standard deviation of the random intercept towards very large values, and by-'subject' slopes rest on the other levels.

The outcome has 9 events and 7 non-events, or 3.5 minority events per fixed-effects column. One of the two classes is absent in 1 of the 4 levels of 'subject', counting the levels with one row, and the median level has 1 minority event.

cases.description: One of five subjects is constant, a share of 20%, below the threshold many, so the threshold any decides: message some.

cases.description: A binomial outcome with the trials column n. A level is constant when all its rows have no events or all have as many events as trials: s1 (2 of 2 and 3 of 3) and s2 (0 of 2 and 0 of 3) are, whereas s3 (2 of 2 and 0 of 3) and s4 (1 of 2 twice) are not. outcome.minority_events sums events and trials, and the median of the five level minority counts 0, 0, 2, 2 and 3 is at position 3.
cases.reason: Inspect the outcome before the model is chosen.
